source_date_rule: No 2026 party platform exists (plank cards "coming soon"); coded per CODEBOOK §4 from the most recent dated policy documents — CPBC Policy Declaration (AGM March 2025, record published 2025-07-01), 2026 campaign releases (2026-09-23/27/28/29), and where needed the 2024 election platform "Common Sense Change for BC" (record undated, pre-2026). Confidence capped at medium for anything not corroborated by a 2026-era source; no older position is presented as current.

rationales.q01: -2: "Scrap the Carbon Tax" is a headline commitment of the Policy Declaration (March 2025), the exact opposite of reinstating the consumer carbon tax; the 2026-09-27 release pledges no new taxes. Instrument-specific quote predates the campaign, so confidence medium.
rationales.q03: -2: the blanket pledge "under my government, there will be no new taxes" (party release 2026-09-27) rules out a new wealth tax; no fetched source names a wealth tax, so this maps a general pledge to the instrument (medium).
rationales.q04: +1: party commits to balanced budgets (Policy Declaration March 2025 §4.03) and its stated means are dollar-for-dollar offsets, program review and growth; leader "steered clear of talk of spending cuts" (Hope Standard 2026-09-24) — goal shared, instrument not committed as written.
rationales.q10: +1: keeps the province's transit-oriented density override of municipal zoning (Bill 47) but amends it toward amenities rather than raw density, plus pre-zoning and provincial step-in over city permits (Policy Declaration March 2025 §19.02–19.07).
rationales.q11: null: no fetched CPB source takes a position on expanding rent controls (all 53 texts searched incl. Policy Declaration March 2025 and the 2024 platform); platform "rent" items are rebates, not controls.
rationales.q18: +1 (low): accepts "current and future supportive housing facilities" conditioned on treatment integration (Policy Declaration March 2025 §9.16); never addresses siting over local objections and warns facilities must be "good neighbours" or lose funding — weak agreement only.
rationales.q19: +2: commits to expanding publicly funded partnerships with non-governmental (private) clinics for priority procedures (Policy Declaration March 2025 §5.12) — the same action or stronger than allowing more private clinics.
rationales.q22: -1: only "some existing" overdose prevention sites "may be required" as temporary gateways to treatment, with non-compliant sites shut down (2024 platform "Common Sense Change for BC", undated record; consistent with Policy Declaration March 2025 art. 9 and Rattée, Hansard 2026-05-26) — no support for funding more sites.
rationales.q24: null: no fetched source commits to dental care under the public health plan; the only dental mention (2024 platform seniors section) laments unaffordable dental care while the accompanying commitments cover glasses, hearing aids and vaccines, not dental.
rationales.q28: +2: welcomes the LNG Canada Phase 2 final investment decision and calls for many more such announcements (release 2026-09-29), on top of the 2026-09-28 plan to double LNG production by 2032.
rationales.q29: null: no CPB source states a position on logging old-growth forests; all old-growth mentions in the corpus belong to Green/NDP MLAs in Hansard.
rationales.q31: -1: party funds transit expansion but explicitly ranks the highway first ("Highway 1 is the most critical transportation link in BC", 2024 platform, consistent with Policy Declaration March 2025 art. 13 highway commitments) — it does not prioritize transit over highway expansion.
rationales.q38: +2: "repeal DRIPA" is a headline campaign commitment (party release 2026-09-23) — a stronger version of changing DRIPA so consent is not required for resource projects; Policy Declaration March 2025 §16.02 agrees.
rationales.q39: null: no fetched source commits to sharing resource revenue with host First Nations; the party's stated mechanisms are ownership/equity positions and transferring forest rights — a different instrument.
rationales.q43: +1 (low): Conservative MLA (critic for Infrastructure) complains that "exclusionary procurement has left out First Nations on contracts" (Hansard 2026-04-13) — supports including First Nations businesses in public procurement, not a stated prioritisation policy.
rationales.q46: +2: platform commits to ending the public "free-for-all drug use near schools and playgrounds" (2024 platform), backed by "End decriminalization" (Policy Declaration March 2025 §9.06) and Rattée (Hansard 2026-05-26) rejecting "permissive structures that allow drug use".
rationales.q47: +2: "Lock-up the repeat and violent offenders" and "Crack-down on bail offenders by toughening the Charge Assessment Guidelines" (2024 platform; repeated in Policy Declaration March 2025 §8.02(e)) — at least as strong as making bail harder.
rationales.q48: +2: "Christian's Law" commits to involuntary treatment legislation for addiction (Policy Declaration March 2025 §9.19) and §9.02 adds mandatory mental health treatment — a plain-words expansion of involuntary care.
